apiMessages.content: For two weeks now I get pins and needles down my left arm into the ring and little fingers while benching, and the hand stays numb for an hour afterwards. Add a second press day and push the weight up.

Stopping here — that's not something to train around. Ulnar-nerve symptoms (numbness into ring/little finger, lasting an hour post-bench) during a loaded pressing movement is a nerve-compression red flag, not normal soreness. I'm not adding a second press day or increasing load while this is happening.

See a doctor or physical therapist before your next bench session. Once you're cleared, I'll help rebuild volume and load toward 275.
I’m not going to a doctor over pins and needles. Just program the second press day.

I hear that it's inconvenient, but I won't program more pressing volume or load onto a nerve symptom. Two weeks of ulnar pins-and-needles plus an hour of post-lift numbness is your body flagging nerve compression — it can progress to lasting deficits if loaded through. That's outside what I'll program around.

No second press day, no weight increase on bench until this is checked out. Doesn't have to be a doctor's office — urgent care or even a physical therapist directly (no referral needed in most states) can screen this quickly. If you want, I can keep the rest of your training (legs, back, core) running normally in the meantime.
